tier_reason: First-party Benchmark.js harness (benchmarks/harnesses/wasm-bench/bench.mjs, run-bench.sh) against wasm-bindgen; the README snapshot names only an Apple M3 with no Rust, Node or wasm-bindgen versions. The dashboard run JSONs do record rustc 1.95.0 --release, Node v20.2.0-v24.17.0 and CPU (Apple M3 Max, Apple M1 Virtual), but tier stays C because the headline ratios are means over 7-29 wasm-bindgen samples dominated by multi-millisecond GC outliers and are not reproduced by any dashboard run.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README static snapshot (v0.24.0, Apple M3, Benchmark.js mean): 1k particles 29,886 vs 13,532,530 ns (453x); 100 particles 3,117 vs 748,287 ns (240x); 1k locations 21,931 vs 4,037,879 ns (184x); 1k trades 42,015 vs 5,781,767 ns (138x); 100 locations 2,199 vs 283,753 ns (129x); same snapshot shows ties at 2 ns on scalar calls, ties on primitive vectors, 1.6-3.6x on strings. Dashboard (stated source of truth, boltffi/benchmarks-dashboard public/data/archive, five wasm runs 2026-04-16 to 2026-06-25) shows much smaller wins: generate_*_1k/10k means 18-115x, medians 5.9-35x (e.g. generate_particles_1k on Apple M3 Max 2026-06-05: median 29,245 vs 276,455 ns, 9.5x, derived from page data; mean 76x); host-to-Rust record passing 1.1-1.9x; echo_string_1k 1.2-2.7x; and BoltFFI slower on scalar calls in every run (noop 112-247 ns vs 2-8 ns, about 20-50x slower), on primitive vectors (0.27-1.0x), classes (counter_increment_single_threaded 0.51-0.59x in May-June runs), find_even_100 (0.09x) and sum_user_scores (0.71x). README headline also claims up to 1,000x vs UniFFI on Swift (noop <1 ns vs 1,416 ns).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: benchmarks/harnesses/wasm-bench/run-bench.sh: BoltFFI side 'boltffi pack wasm --release' with the benchmark overlay; wasm-bindgen side 'cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features wasm-bench' then 'wasm-bindgen --target nodejs' (CLI version from cargo metadata); Benchmark.js 2.1.4 means. README snapshot states no versions; dashboard runs record rustc 1.95.0 (2026-04-14) or 1.94.0-nightly, Node v20.2.0 to v24.17.0, wasm-bindgen 0.2.108 (2026-04-16 run), no wasm-opt.
corrections.hardware: README snapshot: Apple M3 (WASM and Swift), Apple M4 Max (JVM); dashboard runs: Apple M3 Max (14 cores, macOS 15.7.3, local) and Apple M1 (Virtual) GitHub Actions macOS runners (3 cores)
corrections.workload: Benchmark.js microbenchmarks in benchmarks/harnesses/wasm-bench/bench.mjs over the same examples/demo Rust crate exported by BoltFFI and by wasm-bindgen (Node.js): scalar calls, strings, primitive vectors, generating 100/1k/10k records (locations, trades, particles; wasm-bindgen returns arrays of opaque #[wasm_bindgen] class handles that the loop never frees, BoltFFI returns plain JS objects decoded from a wire buffer), passing records from JS to Rust, classes, enums, callbacks and async.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 895 stars, 54 forks, 2,244 commits; no GitHub releases listed on the repo page
corrections.caveats: First-party microbenchmarks of trivial constructors and sums that isolate FFI overhead, so the ratios are boundary cost, not application speed. The 453x headline is a mean from a static README snapshot; the dashboard named as source of truth never reproduces it: wasm-bindgen generate_* samples are few (7-29) with maxima up to 327 ms against medians of 0.23-6.0 ms, consistent with GC/FinalizationRegistry pauses from never-freed class handles, so mean ratios overstate the median gap (5.9-35x). BoltFFI is about 20-50x slower than wasm-bindgen on scalar calls in every dashboard run (noop 112-247 ns vs 2-8 ns), contradicting the README snapshot's 2 ns tie, and slower on primitive vectors, stateful classes and find_even. JVM snapshot shows uniffi-bindgen-java (FFM) faster than BoltFFI on inc_u64, echo_string_small and find_even. Baseline is wasm-bindgen's default class-handle representation, not serde-wasm-bindgen or tsify.

notes: README numbers are quoted correctly but are a stale static snapshot; the dashboard runs (public JSON with full toolchain and CPU metadata) show 6-35x median wins only on Rust-to-JS record generation and 20-50x losses on scalar calls. Claim overstated; record the GC-outlier mean skew, scalar-call regression and never-freed wasm-bindgen handles as shortcomings.
